title: Juniper and the Thorn
premise: Casper Thackeray, once a battle-priest of the silent god Veth, has hidden her magic for twenty years in the warded city of Grayhollow, selling charms that barely work. When the border wards collapse and the stars extinguish, she learns the truth: her god did not die but was devoured by the Thorn, an ancient hunger wearing King Aldric's crown and slowly unmaking the world's memory. Guided by Juniper, a dragon-keeper girl who carries the last living ember of dragon-fire, Casper journeys to the capital to sever the king from the Thorn before his mind—and the world's past—is consumed entirely. In the end, Casper must choose between reclaiming her stolen memories of the god she loved and using them as the blade that frees Aldric; she burns them away, kills the Thorn, and lets a new, quieter magic take root in a world that will have to learn its own name again.
about_author: Wren Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval charm-books before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about forgotten gods, stubborn women, and the cost of remembering.

chapters.title: The Charm-Seller's Quiet
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. In Grayhollow, Casper sells hollow charms to superstitious buyers while hiding the ember of real magic in her palm. A routine day establishes her invisibility, her guilt over Veth's silence, and her rule: never be noticed. Emotional beat: the ache of a life half-lived.

chapters.title: Wards Like Broken Teeth
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. At dusk the border wards shatter with a sound like snapping bone, and the stars go out one by one. Panic floods the city; soldiers sweep for mages. Casper feels her buried power wake violently for the first time in twenty years. Emotional beat: terror and terrible relief.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Carried Fire
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper, sixteen, flees the fallen borderlands carrying a lantern-dragon egg—the last ember of dragon-fire—pursued by gray, faceless riders. Wounded, she collapses into Casper's shop as the riders close in. Emotional beat: desperate trust offered to a stranger.

chapters.title: What the Riders Wanted
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper kills two riders with magic she swore off, discovering they are made of solidified forgetting—they erase what they touch. The egg hatches into a moth-sized dragon that imprints on her. She realizes she cannot stay invisible. Emotional beat: the end of hiding.

chapters.title: A Confessor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper seeks out Brother Hale, her old order's last survivor, now a drunk archivist. He reveals the Thorn's history: it ate Veth from inside the king, and every star snuffed is a memory the world loses forever. Emotional beat: grief reframed as unfinished war.

chapters.title: The Road That Forgets Itself
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The trio leaves Grayhollow along a road where villages have lost their own names. Juniper's fire can restore small memories—a child remembers her mother's lullaby—but each use dims the egg-ember. Emotional beat: hope with a price tag.

chapters.title: Salt and Old Vows
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. At a drowned shrine, Casper relives a suppressed memory: she was Veth's chosen blade, and she abandoned him at the moment of the Thorn's first strike out of fear. Guilt crystallizes into resolve. Emotional beat: self-forgiveness denied, purpose forged.

chapters.title: The Mercenary Company of Last Resort
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. They join a ragtag caravan guarded by mercenaries who remember nothing of their own contracts. Juniper bonds with a scarred sergeant, Tam, showing her gift for restoring others' pasts even as hers stays blank. Emotional beat: found family flickering.

chapters.title: Riders at the Ford
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The gray riders ambush the caravan at a river ford. Casper unleashes her full priest-magic publicly for the first time, burning riders away but revealing herself to spies of the crown. Tam dies holding the line. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: The City That Sold Its Past
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. They reach the capital, Corvenna, where citizens trade memories for bread and the palace glows with stolen starlight. Juniper sees what total forgetting looks like and clutches the dimming ember tighter. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: An Audience With the Hollow King
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Summoned to court, Casper meets King Aldric—and the Thorn behind his eyes recognizes her. It offers her a bargain: her god's memories back, whole, if she surrenders Juniper. She refuses, barely escaping with Hale's help. Emotional beat: temptation survived.

chapters.title: Beneath the Chapel of Roots
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Hidden in the undercity chapel where Veth was first worshipped, Juniper learns her bloodline: dragon-keepers were the god's jailers, sworn to keep the ember that could cut the Thorn free. Her whole orphan life recontextualizes. Emotional beat: inheritance accepted.

chapters.title: Hale's Confession
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Dying of rider-touch wounds, Hale confesses he helped the Thorn enter the king decades ago, believing it would save the order. He gives Casper the rite of Unbinding and dies mid-absolution. Emotional beat: forgiveness given too late to matter, given anyway.

chapters.title: The Ember Fails
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The dragon-ember gutters after Juniper spends it saving a crowd from a palace purge. She believes she has doomed everything and runs, ashamed. Casper finds her and, instead of scolding, tells her the truth of her own cowardice. Emotional beat: despair met with honesty.

chapters.title: What Stars Remember
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. In the dead shrine, Casper performs a forbidden rite: feeding her own memories into the ember to reignite it. She loses her name, her twenty years, her face-knowledge of Juniper—but the flame roars back to life. Emotional beat: sacrifice without applause.

chapters.title: The Palace of Thorns
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper leads a stranger-with-Casper's-face through corridors grown over with black brambles, narrating their shared journey so Casper knows who she is. The dragon grows wings. They breach the throne room as the last star dies. Emotional beat: love as a lamp carried for someone else.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Confrontation with the Thorn, which wears Aldric's body like armor and offers Casper a final vision of Veth alive. She nearly kneels. Juniper's cry—and the ember's heat—call her back. Battle begins across a throne room of thorns and dying light. Emotional beat: the oldest temptation, refused twice.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Casper begins the rite while Juniper shields her with the last dragon-fire, the tiny dragon growing vast enough to burn back the dark. The Thorn tears at Casper's remaining memories; she holds the rite through agony. Emotional beat: endurance as devotion.

chapters.title: The God Who Was Eaten
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The rite splits the Thorn from Aldric, and in the wound Casper glimpses Veth—not dead, dissolved into the world's memories themselves. To kill the Thorn she must burn the ember AND the god's remnants together. She does it, weeping. Emotional beat: killing the thing you love to save what it loved.

chapters.title: Ash and Morning
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The Thorn dies screaming; stars return one by one, each a memory coming home. Aldric, freed and broken, abdicates. Juniper cradles the cold lantern where the dragon slept, mourning, until ash stirs and something new hatches. Emotional beat: grief interrupted by dawn.

chapters.title: A City Learning Its Name
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Months later, Grayhollow repeals its magic laws. Casper, still missing her stolen years, opens a school of small honest charms with Juniper. A student asks if the god is gone; Casper says the world is what's left of him. Emotional beat: peace built on absence.

chapters.title: Juniper and the Thorn
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. On the anniversary, Juniper and Casper plant a thornbush over the old shrine—remembering the enemy, not erasing it. The young dragon lands on the branches and the bush flowers out of season. Juniper writes the first page of the keepers' new ledger. Emotional beat: inheritance renewed, memory chosen rather than suffered.
